descriptions.title: Why ACE-Step replaced MusicGen
descriptions.body: PersonalSong began on HuggingFace MusicGen, which only produced ~30-second INSTRUMENTAL tracks — it could not sing the recipient's name, which is the entire point of a personalized song. The pipeline was rebuilt around ACE-Step, a local diffusion singing model that performs a full song (verse/chorus/bridge) with sung vocals directly from lyrics + style tags, on the local GPU in bfloat16 at zero marginal cost. ace_engine.py loads the pipeline once as a thread-locked singleton and keeps it resident in VRAM. The README still describes the old MusicGen/Suno route; the live engine is ACE-Step (model_used 'ACE-Step 0.2.0' in song metadata).

descriptions.title: think:false + name-injection — making the LLM cooperate
descriptions.body: Two hard-won fixes make local lyric generation reliable. First, qwen3-style models spend their token budget on internal <think> reasoning and return an EMPTY lyric body; the Ollama call sets think=False so the model emits lyrics directly, and any <think> blocks that slip through are stripped (lyrics.py + ace_engine.normalize_lyrics). Second, LLMs writing in non-English languages frequently address the recipient without ever using their literal name — defeating the gift. ensure_name_in_lyrics() guarantees the name is actually sung by injecting it as a vocative ('Name, ...') into the chorus and first verse if it's absent, with a sung-hook fallback if the lyrics have no usable line. The prompt also demands the exact name appear at least twice including the chorus.

descriptions.title: Sing the name correctly — pronunciation without corrupting the lyrics
descriptions.body: Names are often mis-sung, especially across languages. PersonalSong keeps a per-language pronunciation dictionary (config/pronunciations.json) of phonetic respellings. At generation time apply_pronunciation() swaps the name for its respelling ONLY in the text fed to the singing model, while the displayed and saved lyrics keep the real spelling. Users can teach a respelling by recording the name (Whisper transcribes it and suggests a syllable-hyphenated respelling), preview how it will sound spoken in the target language (edge-tts), edit it, and reuse it across future songs.

descriptions.title: GPU contention — one model at a time
descriptions.body: ACE-Step, Demucs, Seed-VC, Whisper and SDXL all want the GPU, and the box has one card. The design serializes and isolates them: ACE-Step generation runs in a single-worker ThreadPoolExecutor so two requests never fight the GPU; before each run the app asks Ollama to unload its model (keep_alive=0) to free VRAM; Demucs gender-detection is forced onto the CPU so it doesn't thrash the resident ACE-Step; Seed-VC runs in its own venv as a subprocess (incompatible deps + its own VRAM lifecycle); and SDXL-Turbo cover art runs in a subprocess that frees VRAM on exit. This avoids the OOM/timeout thrashing that GPU contention caused.

descriptions.title: The FFmpeg / TorchCodec / cu128 gotcha
descriptions.body: On torch 2.11, torchaudio.load/save routes through TorchCodec, which needs FFmpeg *shared* DLLs that aren't on a stock Windows box. PersonalSong vendors an FFmpeg 7.1 shared build under ffmpeg_shared/ and env_setup.ensure_ffmpeg_on_path() prepends it to PATH on import (subprocesses inherit it), so Demucs and Seed-VC don't fail with 'libtorchcodec_core7.dll could not be loaded'. As a belt-and-braces measure, ace_engine monkey-patches torchaudio.save to write via soundfile (libsndfile, no external FFmpeg). A second, separate gyan FFmpeg build (with libcdio) is resolved on demand only for audio-CD ripping.

descriptions.title: Seed-VC voice cloning — two modes, isolated venv
descriptions.body: Voice conversion has two distinct uses. For a full cover, cover.py isolates the target singer's vocal (Demucs), isolates the ACE-Step song's vocal (Demucs again), then runs Seed-VC with --f0-condition True (pitch-aware, required for singing) to re-sing the ACE vocal in the target voice, and mixes it over the chosen instrumental. For a spoken dedication, voice_clone.py re-voices the edge-tts speech with --f0-condition False (speech, not sung). In both cases Seed-VC lives in seed-vc/.venv and is driven as a subprocess because its dependencies collide with ACE-Step's, and it manages its own GPU memory.

descriptions.title: Resilient by design — optional steps never fail the song
descriptions.body: The creative core is offline and must always succeed; everything else is best-effort. Plex sync, YouTube Music upload, the spoken dedication, MP3 transcode, and cover art are each wrapped so a failure is swallowed and logged rather than aborting the request — a missing Plex token or an offline YT Music account never costs the user their song. ACE-Step output is normalized whether it writes .wav or .flac, and the WAV is kept if transcode fails. The whole studio runs as the QI_PersonalSong NSSM service (loopback-only, port 8088) so it's always available without exposing anything to the internet.
